#### `paths_under`

It may not stop: it calls itself. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn paths_under(c: Category, above: list[string]) -> list[string]
  let here = above.append(c.name)
  c.items.map(i => here.append(i.name).join(" / ")).concat(c.children.flat_map(x => paths_under(c: x, above: here)))
```

#### `pruned`

It may not stop: it calls itself. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn pruned(c: Category) -> Category?
  let kept = c.children.filter_map(x => pruned(c: x))
  if c.items.count() = 0 and kept.count() = 0 then none else Category { ..c, children: kept }
```

fn relabel(c: Category, label: (string) -> string) -> Category

## Examples

`kaname check` runs each line of `examples` in the reference interpreter, as a host would call the function, and compares the answer with the one written. The reference interpreter answers these.

```kn
paths(c: Category { name: "Garden", items: [], children: [Category { name: "Tools", items: [Item { sku: "sp-1", name: "Spade", price: 1999USDc }], children: [] }] })
  = ["Garden / Tools / Spade"]
pruned(c: Category { name: "Garden", items: [], children: [Category { name: "Seeds", items: [], children: [] }] })
  = none
slugged(c: Category { name: "Garden Tools", items: [], children: [Category { name: "Hand Trowels", items: [], children: [] }] })
  = Category { name: "garden-tools", items: [], children: [Category { name: "hand-trowels", items: [], children: [] }] }
names(c: Category { name: "Garden", items: [], children: [Category { name: "Tools", items: [], children: [] }, Category { name: "Seeds", items: [], children: [] }] })
  = ["Garden", "Tools", "Seeds"]
```
